Our organ's cells need oxygen to function. Organs fail when cells lack oxygen.

Do the cells have enough oxygen? Are interventions necessary? How effective are they? In many
situations only signs of damage allow physicians to answer these questions with confidence - when it
is too late.

Now there finally is a way to measure oxygen inside active cells. This is quite different from
current measurements in blood. Only in the cells themselves can it be determined if there is enough
oxygen or if cells are hypoxic - and also if cells can't use the oxygen they receive.

# COMET MEASUREMENT SYSTEM

[CL8A3769]

The [CE-marked][6] COMET measurement system determines oxygen availability as partial pressure of
oxygen [mmHg]. It non-invasively measures oxygen in human skin cells with a high concentration of
protoporphyrin IX - in real time at the bedside and only in the mitochondria of active cells.

The COMET measurement system and its prototypes have been used in 16 clinical trials at seven
institutes in two countries, in intensive care patients as well as during and after cardiopulmonary
bypass and other major surgeries. The effects of hemoglobin, temperature, flow, blood pressure
management and other interventions on cellular oxygenation are visible in real time. Studies
demonstrated how cellular oxygen provides more relevant information than previously available
measures like lactate, regional saturation or blood pressure. Additional clinical trials are
expected to start enrolling soon.

We expect that the measurement of oxygen in the cells will enable doctors to guide the many
interventions to ensure oxygen delivery to cells and that this will make care easier, safer and
cheaper.  Skin is regarded as an early warning sensor, so should give physicians time to prevent
lasting damage. Preclinically, transfusion need was detected two hours before kidney failure.
Monitoring cellular oxygen in skin should therefore provide early warning of complications and allow
doctors to assess the necessity for interventions and follow their effects in real time. It should
also facilitate decisions before and during peripheral interventions and be useful to detect
alterations of cellular metabolism  and help develop treatments for metabolic dysfunction.
Measurements have also been performed in the gut of volunteers and preclinically in other organs. So
far, a CE marked sensor is only available for the skin. Eventually, images of cellular oxygen
distributions in organs should help assess tissue function for diagnosis, interventions or wound
care.

Use the COMET measurement system as a low-burden adjunct to your studies and improve patient safety.
[Contact us for a quote][7] (Europe only).

## THE SCIENCE OF CELLULAR MONITORING

Anesthesiologist Dr. Egbert Mik, building on his invention made together with Dr. Michiel
Sinaasappel, developed the *protoporphyrin IX triplet state lifetime technique (PpIX-TSLT). *It is
the first practical way to clinically measure oxygen availability and consumption where oxygen is
needed: in the tissue cells rather than in the blood. It uses the oxygen dependent duration of the
'glow-in-the-dark' of the precursor to heme. This protoporphyrin IX is metabolized in epidermal
mitochondria after local priming with aminolevulinic acid used in photodynamic therapy or diagnosis.
The signal therefore originates only in active mitochondria and reflects the [balance between oxygen
supply][8] and demand. The COMET's skin sensor collects a signal from several square millimeters of
epidermis, providing an average value for the different cells. In a preclinical trial the
oxygenation of cells in the gut has been measured with an endoscopic sensor. Ultimately,
interstitial probes, even imaging, should be feasible with this technology. Oxygen should be
measured where it is needed so doctors can treat what matters.

## A Safe & Effective Solution For Diagnosed Skin Conditions

### Phothera is the leading manufacturer of FDA-cleared narrowband home phototherapy devices for
### chronic skin conditions, with more than 80 years of experience helping patients take steps to
### treat their chronic skin conditions.

## Phototherapy for Chronic Skin Conditions

Narrowband ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) phototherapy is a first-line treatment for psoriasis, vitiligo,
and Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL), and an important treatment option for eczema (atopic
dermatitis) when topical or biologic therapies are not enough.

Phothera helps make this treatment available both at home and in your doctor’s office.

### **Different conditions.** **One trusted treatment that fits your life.**

[Learn About Phototherapy][24]

## Phototherapy, the Way It Should Be Prescribed

Phothera delivers clinically studied phototherapy devices designed to support both at-home treatment
and in-office settings to best fit your needs.

### At-Home Phototherapy
* Prescribed by your dermatologist and designed for safe home treatment
* Enabled with the ClearLink****^{®}**** Controller with Guided Mode technology designed to support
  safe, accurate, and effective treatment
* Up to 3x higher treatment completion rates compared with standard home phototherapy. (LITE Study,
  n=783)¹
* Convenient and easy to fit into daily life
* Broad insurance coverage with **$0 cost for eligible patients***

*$0 patient cost applies to eligible insured patients. Not all patients will qualify.

### Phototherapy Administered in Office
* Covered by most major insurance providers
* Clinical phototherapy solutions designed for multiple chronic skin conditions and treatment areas
* National dermatology treatment guidelines recommended

### **The same proven narrowband UVB therapy.**

### **Delivered where it works best for you.**

# Welcome to Phototherapy Perth

The arrival of your baby is joyful, yet hearing they have neonatal jaundice can be stressful. You’re
not alone—jaundice causes 71% of preterm infant readmissions. Now, for the first time in WA, we
offer phototherapy blanket rentals, a proven treatment that lets your baby recover at home, avoiding
prolonged hospitalization or repeated doctor visits. Our mission is to provide accessible,
effective, and comfortable care for families facing neonatal jaundice.

## Using Phototherapy to Treat Jaundice in Neonates

For over 30 years, phototherapy has been the gold-standard non-invasive treatment for neonatal
jaundice. Blue light waves break down excess bilirubin, safely reducing yellowing of skin and eyes.
While hospitals traditionally use overhead UV lights, our phototherapy blankets offer adjustable
intensity—allowing continuous, doctor-approved home treatment until bilirubin levels normalize.
* ## Your baby must be close to full term
* ## They must be at least 48 hours old
* ## Other than having jaundice, your baby must be medically well, and will be checked by the baby
  ## doctor to ensure they are suitable for phototherapy at home.
* ## You will need to speak to a nurse from the Hospital in the Home team
* ## And finally, you’ll need to have a feeding plan in place for your baby. Your midwife or
  ## Paediatrician will talk about this.

Your child’s doctor will look for signs of jaundice, and ask questions about birth weight, weight
gain and feeding.

A screening test with a specialised light called a transcutaneous bilirubinometer is sometimes used
on your baby’s chest to get an approximate measure of the jaundice.

A blood test to measure the level of bilirubin in your baby’s blood, called serum bilirubin level
(SBR), may be ordered. This is the most accurate way to measure an SBR and involves collecting a
small amount of blood from the arm, hand or heel. Additional blood tests or urine tests may be
ordered if there is evidence your baby’s jaundice is caused by an underlying disorder that will need
treatment.

**Treatment**

Mild jaundice often goes away without treatment, however babies with high levels of bilirubin may
need treatment. Treatment may include phototherapy, exchange transfusion or medication.

## Using Phototherapy to Treat Jaundice in Neonates

For over 30 years, phototherapy has been the gold-standard non-invasive treatment for neonatal
jaundice. Blue light waves break down excess bilirubin, safely reducing yellowing of skin and eyes.
While hospitals traditionally use overhead UV lights, our phototherapy blankets offer adjustable
intensity—allowing continuous, doctor-approved home treatment until bilirubin levels normalize.

The information on this website is for healthcare professionals. The COMET system is only offered to
European hospitals or researchers with applicable approvals.

Our organ's cells need oxygen to function. Organs fail when cells lack oxygen.

Do the cells have enough oxygen? Are interventions necessary? How effective are they? In many
situations only signs of damage allow physicians to answer these questions with confidence - when it
is too late.

Now there finally is a way to measure oxygen inside active cells. This is quite different from
current measurements in blood. Only in the cells themselves can it be determined if there is enough
oxygen or if cells are hypoxic - and also if cells can't use the oxygen they receive.

# COMET MEASUREMENT SYSTEM

[CL8A3769]

The [CE-marked][6] COMET measurement system determines oxygen availability as partial pressure of
oxygen [mmHg]. It non-invasively measures oxygen in human skin cells with a high concentration of
protoporphyrin IX - in real time at the bedside and only in the mitochondria of active cells.

The COMET measurement system and its prototypes have been used in 16 clinical trials at seven
institutes in two countries, in intensive care patients as well as during and after cardiopulmonary
bypass and other major surgeries. The effects of hemoglobin, temperature, flow, blood pressure
management and other interventions on cellular oxygenation are visible in real time. Studies
demonstrated how cellular oxygen provides more relevant information than previously available
measures like lactate, regional saturation or blood pressure. Additional clinical trials are
expected to start enrolling soon.

We expect that the measurement of oxygen in the cells will enable doctors to guide the many
interventions to ensure oxygen delivery to cells and that this will make care easier, safer and
cheaper.  Skin is regarded as an early warning sensor, so should give physicians time to prevent
lasting damage. Preclinically, transfusion need was detected two hours before kidney failure.
Monitoring cellular oxygen in skin should therefore provide early warning of complications and allow
doctors to assess the necessity for interventions and follow their effects in real time. It should
also facilitate decisions before and during peripheral interventions and be useful to detect
alterations of cellular metabolism  and help develop treatments for metabolic dysfunction.
Measurements have also been performed in the gut of volunteers and preclinically in other organs. So
far, a CE marked sensor is only available for the skin. Eventually, images of cellular oxygen
distributions in organs should help assess tissue function for diagnosis, interventions or wound
care.

Use the COMET measurement system as a low-burden adjunct to your studies and improve patient safety.
[Contact us for a quote][7] (Europe only).

Sinaasappel, developed the *protoporphyrin IX triplet state lifetime technique (PpIX-TSLT). *It is
the first practical way to clinically measure oxygen availability and consumption where oxygen is
needed: in the tissue cells rather than in the blood. It uses the oxygen dependent duration of the
'glow-in-the-dark' of the precursor to heme. This protoporphyrin IX is metabolized in epidermal
mitochondria after local priming with aminolevulinic acid used in photodynamic therapy or diagnosis.
The signal therefore originates only in active mitochondria and reflects the [balance between oxygen
supply][8] and demand. The COMET's skin sensor collects a signal from several square millimeters of
epidermis, providing an average value for the different cells. In a preclinical trial the
oxygenation of cells in the gut has been measured with an endoscopic sensor. Ultimately,
interstitial probes, even imaging, should be feasible with this technology. Oxygen should be
measured where it is needed so doctors can treat what matters.

#### [What is light therapy, and how does it help chronic skin conditions at Array Skin?][40]

calm inflammation, reduce itching, slow skin cell overgrowth, and stimulate pigment production. It
is a leading treatment for eczema, psoriasis, and vitiligo, offering a safe, drug-free alternative
to topical steroids and systemic medications.

Array Skin began offering narrowband UVB therapy in Orange County and Los Angeles and is expanding
access through franchised clinics in select U.S. markets, bringing this specialized clinical service
to patients who may otherwise face significant barriers to care.

# About Cutaneous Lymphoma

Our Vision
A Life Free From the Burdens of Cutaneous Lymphomas
Welcome to the Cutaneous Lymphoma Foundation where we believe knowledge is power!
WHAT IS CUTANEOUS LYMPHOMA?

Cutaneous lymphomas are cancers of lymphocytes (a type of white blood cells) that primarily involve
the skin. Cutaneous lymphomas are classified based on whether they are cancers of B-lymphocytes
(B-cell) or T-lymphocytes (T-cell).

## CUTANEOUS T-CELL LYMPHOMA (CTCL)

Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) is the most common type of cutaneous lymphoma, and typically
presents with red, scaly patches or plaques on the skin. Itching is common, with more than 80% of
people with CTCL reporting they have itch. CTCL often mimics eczema, psoriasis, or other chronic
dermatitis, and because of this it’s common that the diagnosis of CTCL is delayed, sometimes by
years or decades. Only a minority of people with CTCL develop advanced disease, with tumor
formation, ulceration, involvement of lymph nodes, blood, and internal organs. Most people with CTCL
have indolent (i.e. chronic, slowly growing) lymphomas – treatable, but not curable, and usually not
life-threatening.

## CUTANEOUS B-CELL LYMPHOMAS (CBCL)

Cutaneous B-cell lymphomas (CBCL) make up about 20-25% of all cutaneous lymphomas, and are cancers
that develop from skin-based B-cells.  There are 3 main types of CBCL; primary cutaneous follicle
center (“follicular”) lymphoma, primary cutaneous marginal zone (“MALT”) lymphoma, and primary
cutaneous diffuse large B-cell (DLBCL, “leg type”) lymphoma. Primary cutaneous follicle center and
primary cutaneous marginal zone lymphomas are the most common forms of CBCL, and are slow growing or
indolent types that respond well to mild treatments. Systemic or nodal B-cell lymphomas can
secondarily involve the skin, and when a skin biopsy shows B-cell lymphoma it is very important to
make sure that the lymphoma is truly coming from the skin and not from a systemic lymphoma that has
spread to the skin.  

For a more in depth overview, watch [Cutaneous Lymphoma 101][82].

Mycosis fungoides is the most common form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL). Mycosis fungoides”

# Primary Cutaneous B-cell Lymphoma

Primary cutaneous B-cell lymphomas (CBCLs) are a cutaneous lymphoma (a cancer of white blood cells)
that affects B-cells in the skin. Learn more about the diagnosis, variants, treatment options and
prognosis of CBCLs.
* [Read more][86]

# Lymphomatoid Papulosis

Lymphomatoid Papulosis (LyP) is a disorder of the immune system that manifests with self-healing
small bumps and spots on the skin that come and go. Learn more about how LyP is diagnosed, treated
and its prognosis.
* [Read more][87]

# PRIMARY CUTANEOUS ANAPLASTIC LARGE CELL LYMPHOMA

Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphomas (CTCL) are part of a group of rare non-Hodgkin lymphomas that
arise from the T-cell type lymphocytes. Learn more about how it is diagnosed, the variants,
treatments and prognosis.
* [Read more][88]

# Folliculotropic mycosis fungoides

Mycosis fungoides  (MF) is the most common form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Folliculotropic
mycosis fungoides (FMF) is a subtype of MF that involves hair follicles.
* [Read more][89]

# Discover the Power of Light Therapy.

Narrowband ultraviolet B light therapy (NB-UVB) has helped improve the quality of life and outcomes
in patients with chronic skin conditions for decades.  
[Book a 10-Min Discovery Call ][37] [Explore the Science ][38]
discover more [scroll]
[fav]

## 
## Supporting People with Autoimmune Conditions and Skin Disorders Driven by Inflammation

From translational research in acute COVID, MS fatigue, and chronic skin conditions, light therapy
offers a non-drug option your doctor can prescribe to calm your immune system.
* Patients
  If your immune system is in chronic overdrive, light therapy may help.
* Caregivers
  We support your role in guiding care and empowering informed decisions.
* Physicians
  For providers exploring complementary options grounded in research.
[Explore the Science ][39]

## How It Works

Our skin is specifically tuned to absorb NB-UVB light, which starts a natural cascade of actions
that calms the immune system and reduces inflammation for better health. Cytokind partners with you
and your care provider to make this light therapy treatment accessible at home.
* **NB-UVB Safety and Efficacy**
  NB-UVB light therapy has been used safely for decades, with a long track record in dermatology of
  effectively treating many conditions.
* **Prescribed by Your Care Provider**
  The purchase of these lights requires a prescription from your care provider. Cytokind is here to
  help.
[GettyImages-1635844476]
* **What You’ll Experience**
  The therapy starts with very short sessions—usually less than a minute per side each day—and
  gradually increases to about four minutes per side over a month, becoming an easy part of your
  daily routine and ongoing health maintenance.
* Ongoing Support
  From device delivery to daily use, we make sure you’re not on your own.
[Explore the Science ][40]

# Syntonic Equipment Options

Our portables hold two sets of filters (single, double, or triple) at a time. Watch this short video

## EyeLux **Portables **
* *Provide the power of in-office quality syntonics…in the home.*

  ***Power ****of Glass *
  
  ***Accurate ****CSO Transmissions *
  
  ***Quality**** of Volk Condensing Lenses*
* *Each unit is designed to contain 2 filter combinations (single, double, triple). Switch out
  filters under a minute’s time via a simple process. Click on picture above for brief video.*
* *Unauthorized use of the unit is prevented by a secure ****passcode**** that only you and your
  staff have access to. *
* *A built-in digital timer allows session duration to be custom set before sending home. *
* *Compliance monitored via a built in digital activity log.*
* *Gentle modulation of the light brightness provides continuous re-engagement of attention by the
  nervous system for added effectiveness. Participants love this ! Spitler promoted it!*

## EyeLux **In-Office**
* *The instrument contains 8 filter combinations chosen at the touch of the computer tablet. *
* *The glass filters remain protected from exposure to environment and human hands. *
* *Gentle modulation of the light brightness provides continuous re-engagement of attention by the
  nervous system for added effectiveness. Participants love this! Spitler promoted it!*
* *Pay monthly instead of purchasing. *
* *Return and end use anytime. *
* *Never worry about costly repairs or outdated technology. *
* *Comes standard with 8 filter combinations including the Miracle Workers: A/O, A/D, M/D, M/U, U/O
  Pi/O, D/O, N. *
* *Designed to attach to any commercially made computer arm.* Choose from a rolling kioske or a
  desktop option.

**Only EyeLux has products being used in university studies.**

The first-ever automatic computerized syntonic instrument. Efficacy and efficiency together.

* Like watching syntonics on steroids! *

  *[***MST***][32]* (aka *[***OMST***][33]***)****. *
* * Without question, this is a ****“game-changer”**** tool; inspired by the Sensory Learning
  Program. Thank you Mary Bolles.*
* *A unique subcortical therapy technique using syntonic phototherapy, vestibular stimulation,
  proprioception, auditory stimulation simultaneously in a safe and controlled clinically proven
  environment. *
* *Guides the entrainment of sensory regulation resulting in enhanced filtering and prioritizing of
  sensory information coming into the brain from the environment. *
* *The brain will then engage much better in further traditional top-down therapies including vision
  therapy. *
* *Facilitates childhood sensory processing development to help overcome autism spectrum disorders,
  ADHD, learning difficulties*
* *Accelerates post concussion vision rehabilitation*
* *Enhances other intervention outcomes including vision therapy.*
* *We now have 30 locations! *

## כמשל מעולם הצומח

### „ כפי שצמח זקוק לקרקע פורייה, שורשים בריאים, גזע עמיד וענפים שיאפשרו צמיחת פירות, כך גם שיערך.
### לכן, אנו דואגים לבריאות הקרקפת, שורש השערה וגוף השערה גם יחד לטובת עידוד צמיחת השיער ובריאותו "

## אבחון טריקולוגי

השלב הראשון מתחיל באבחון טריקולוגי מקצועי באמצעות מיכשור מתקדם. האבחון אינו פולשני וללא כאבים.
באמצעות בדיקה מיקרוסקופית אנו בודקים את בריאות גוף השיערה, שורש השיערה, בריאות הקרקפת ופרמטרים
נוספים במטרה למפות במדוייק את המצב הקיים ואת הטיפול האפקטיבי הנדרש להשבת בריאות שיערך והכל באופן
מדוייק ומותאם אישית עבורך.

## פתרונות טיפול

הטיפול בהייר קליניק מותאם אישית ומטרתו לייצר איזון מקסימלי בעור הקרקפת ושורשי השיער. אנו משתמשים
במגוון שיטות טיפול מתקדמות כגון טיפול ביוקפילרי לאיזון והזנת הקרקפת, זריקות PRP, מיקרונידלינג,
פוטותרפיה, אלקטרותרפיה, הדמיית זקיקי שיער לנשים, השתלות שיער לנשים ושרות משלים-טיפול של סלון לעיצוב
ושיקום השיער. הטיפול כולל שימוש בתכשירים מתקדמים שיעילותם הוכחה במחקרים קליניים ומאושרים ע"י משרד
הבריאות.

## סלון בריאות

סלון הבריאות הוקם במטרה להעניק לשיערך, כחלק משירות משלים-טיפול, את המראה הבריא והמחמיא ביותר. כל
הטיפולים בסלון בריאים, בדגש על שמירת טיב השערה וטיפול נכון בצבע לשיער וכן שמירה על ערכים אקולוגיים.
מספרת הבריאות היא הדרך שלנו להבטיח שמירה על תוצאות הטיפול ושתראי נהדר והכל בהתאמה אישית לצרכייך. תני
לנו להמשיך ולהעניק לשיערך מראה בריא, מלא נפח ומושלם גם בגמר הטיפול

## הסיפור שלנו

כשמדובר בשיער שלך את צריכה את הטובים והמנוסים ביותר. אנדרי בניטה, מנכ"ל, בעלים-שותף. קארין אלבכרי,
טריקולוגית ראשית, בעלים-שותף. מובילים את הייר קליניק כבר 30 שנה, בפריסה ארצית, להישגים חסרי תקדים
בתחום טיפולי השיער והקרקפת בישראל ובעולם. ידע וניסיון הובילו הייר קליניק למחקר ופיתוח תכשירים
טיפוליים ייחודיים ומתקדמים עם מרכיבים פורצי דרך בתעשייה העולמית. הייר קליניק חברה באיגוד הטריקולוגיה
הבינלאומי, IAT, ומקיימת עמו קשרים שוטפים, משתפת מידע עם חבריו ברחבי העולם, משתתפת בכנסים עולמיים
ועורכת ימי עיון והדרכה לטריקולוגים רבים בארץ ובעולם. קארין אלבכרי היא יו"ר הדירקטוריון של ארגון
הטריקולוגיה העולמי.

## Red Light Therapy Mats

ShineNova [red light therapy mats][66] ( blankets and bags) are flexible devices that incorporate
LEDs to combine red light (660 nm) and near-infrared light (850 nm). These mats provide
non-invasive, full-body, or targeted therapy for pain relief, muscle recovery, and skin health. They
offer greater convenience than rigid panels, allowing users to lie down or sit directly on the mat
for extended sessions, which maximizes light absorption through direct skin contact. Crafted from
premium materials, these mats feature a transparent TPU cover film for added comfort, and they are
waterproof, sweat-resistant, and easy to clean. The inclusion of fire-retardant materials enhances

# **On a mission to make the world safer, healthier and more productive**

#### Madison Industries is one of the largest and most successful privately held companies in the
#### world. Madison builds entrepreneurially driven, branded market leaders that are committed to
#### making the world safer, healthier and more productive by creating innovative solutions that
#### deliver outstanding customer value. The team at Madison is committed to building something
#### truly remarkable that long outlasts them while coaching others to reach their highest
#### potential.

[About us][28]

## How Do We Do This?

By creating an entrepreneurial safe haven in an environment of trust where leaders with a bias for
action can thrive.

[SEE OUR IMPACT][29]

###### Filtration Group

## Discovering new paths to good health

Filtration Group is responsible for breakthrough solutions that advance a healthier society on a
global scale. They purify the air we breathe, filter the water we drink, make our hospitals safer,
reduce carbon emissions and enhance the effectiveness of medical devices. Their solutions protect
our loved ones from harmful elements and give us peace of mind.

[SEE how][30]
* As an entrepreneur who built his business from scratch, I was looking for the perfect partner to
  help me grow what I was still very passionate about building. Madison is truly that perfect
  partner to assist us in our journey; incredibly helpful and unbelievably responsive.
  
  Todd Younggreen, Founder & CEO, TTI

###### Task force tips

## Saving Lives and Protecting Property

For as long as there have been fire pumps, firefighters have had difficulty obtaining the correct
pressure from firehoses. Task Force Tips created a nozzle that adapts to varying degrees of pressure
— making it safer and easier for firefighters to do their jobs. It’s a small component that has made
a huge impact and helped countless firefighters save lives.

[SEE How][31]
* Our business is making the world safer, healthier and more productive by creating unparalleled
  filtration products.
  
  George Nolen, Chairman, Filtration Group

###### Drucker Diagnostics

## **Getting You and Your Doctor the Correct Results Faster**

Drucker Diagnostics improves blood processing systems by delivering accurate results quicker and at
a reduced cost.

[SEE how][32]
* Drucker had been in the family for decades and we had no intention of selling our company. In
  fact, Madison seeks business owners that are not looking to sell. They want passionate
  entrepreneurs who want to continue to build. So they create an environment that allows you to
  continue to do what you enjoy doing. We are now positioned to grow significantly and capitalize on
  opportunities we could not have otherwise accomplished. Our best days are ahead of us!
  
  Craig Stout, Group President, Madison Medical
* As an entrepreneur who built his business from scratch, I was looking for the perfect partner to
  help me grow what I was still very passionate about building. Madison is truly that perfect
  partner to assist us in our journey; incredibly helpful and unbelievably responsive.
  
  Todd Younggreen, Founder & CEO, TTI

If you crave an environment that allows you to lean forward, challenge the status quo and connect

Wir, die Schulze & Böhm GmbH, sind mit den weltweit führenden medisun UV- und Lichtsystemen seit
über 34 Jahren der Partner für Dermatologen in Praxen und Kliniken. Die umfangreiche Produktpalette
reicht vom kompakten **medisun Psori-Kamm** über verschiedene Teilbestrahlungsgeräte bis zu
anspruchsvollen Ganzkörper-Therapie-Systemen der Extraklasse. Dazu zählen insbesondere die
UV-Kabinen **medisun 2800 Innovation**, die **medisun PDT Systeme** und die **medisun XENIA** UVA-1
Liege mit ihrer innovativen Energiespartechnologie und ihren vielfältigen Funktionen. Nicht nur das
**medisun XENIA UVA-1** System ist weltweit konkurrenzlos, sondern auch viele weitere Innovationen
aus unserem Hause!  Hautkrankheiten, wie Psoriasis, Neurodermitis, Vitiligo, weißer Hautkrebs
(aktinische Keratosen), Sklerodermie und andere Autoimmunerkrankungen, können heute erfolgreich und
optimiert mit medisun-Therapiesystemen behandelt werden. Alle medisun Systeme stammen aus eigener
Entwicklung und werden **„Made in Germany“** in unserem Werk in Brühl produziert. Medisun-Produkte
erfüllen höchste Qualitätsansprüche und sind als Medizinprodukte CE-zertifiziert.

Die Software für die medisun UV- und Lichtsysteme und das netzwerkfähige
Medisoft-Therapiemanagementsystem wird komplett in unserem Haus von erfahrenen Ingenieuren
entwickelt. medisun-Produkte sind weltweit bekannt für hervorragende Behandlungserfolge, einfache
Bedienung und langlebige Qualität.

Kundenservice steht für uns an erster Stelle. Neben unserem werkseigenen Kundendienst stehen Ihnen
auch unsere geschulten Servicepartner in über 34 Ländern zur Verfügung.

Narrowband ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) phototherapy is a first-line treatment for psoriasis, vitiligo,
and Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL), and an important treatment option for eczema (atopic
dermatitis) when topical or biologic therapies are not enough.

Phothera helps make this treatment available both at home and in your doctor’s office.

### **Different conditions.** **One trusted treatment that fits your life.**

and in-office settings to best fit your needs.

* Broad insurance coverage with **$0 cost for eligible patients***

* National dermatology treatment guidelines recommended

# Narrowband UVB Phototherapy Treatment: Safe, Effective, & Versatile

Phothera is the leading manufacturer of FDA-cleared home and clinical use narrowband phototherapy
devices for chronic skin conditions. The company was formed through the merger of Daavlin and
National Biological Corporation (NatBio), both unified under [Madison Industries][48] — a global
industrial leader dedicated to building brands that are safer, healthier, and built for long-term
growth. Phothera brings over 80 years of combined phototherapy experience.

## Bring Proven Phototherapy into Modern Dermatology Workflows

Dermatologists have relied on narrowband ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) phototherapy for decades to treat
psoriasis, vitiligo, and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL), where it remains a first-line therapy in
the American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) guidelines. For atopic dermatitis (eczema), phototherapy
is an important option when topical treatments are not enough.

Phothera helps make prescribing and managing phototherapy simple with tools, like convenient EMR
integrations and digital prescription submissions, designed to support you, your practice, and your
patients.

## Why Dermatologists Choose NB-UVB Phototherapy with Phothera

Reduce reliance on systemic medications:

A medication-free treatment option for psoriasis, vitiligo, CTCL, and atopic dermatitis.

Improved adherence with home phototherapy:

Guided Mode devices include protocols with built-in safety guardrails and demonstrated 3x higher
adherence in the 783-patient LITE clinical trial.¹

Simplify prescribing and workflow:

Compatible with Epic and EMA to support prescribing and documentation.

Expanded patient access and coverage:

Broad insurance coverage with $0 cost for eligible patients, helping remove financial barriers to
treatment.

## Phototherapy can be administered in-office or at-home, making it a versatile & widely adaptable
## treatment choice.

## At-Home Phototherapy
* Designed for safe home treatment
* Guided Mode technology with on-device app and** safety protocols built in**
* **3x higher adherence compared with standard home therapy **(LITE Study, n=783)¹
* Broad insurance coverage with **$0 cost for eligible patients***
* **EMR-compatible prescribing with EMA**^{®}**, Epic^{®}, and most other major dermtology EMRs**

*$0 patient cost applies to eligible insured patients. Not all patients will qualify.

[START PRESCRIBING][49]

## In-Office Phototherapy
* Clinical phototherapy devices designed for dermatology practices
* Also covered by most major insurance providers
* Expand treatment offerings within your practice
* Recommended in national dermatology treatment guidelines

The same proven Narrowband UVB therapy your patients trust–delivered where it works best for your
patient.

## Using Phototherapy to Treat Jaundice in Neonates

For over 30 years, phototherapy has been the gold-standard non-invasive treatment for neonatal
jaundice. Blue light waves break down excess bilirubin, safely reducing yellowing of skin and eyes.
While hospitals traditionally use overhead UV lights, our phototherapy blankets offer adjustable
intensity—allowing continuous, doctor-approved home treatment until bilirubin levels normalize.
* ## Your baby must be close to full term
* ## They must be at least 48 hours old
* ## Other than having jaundice, your baby must be medically well, and will be checked by the baby
  ## doctor to ensure they are suitable for phototherapy at home.
* ## You will need to speak to a nurse from the Hospital in the Home team
* ## And finally, you’ll need to have a feeding plan in place for your baby. Your midwife or
  ## Paediatrician will talk about this.

## How is it diagnosed?

Your child’s doctor will look for signs of jaundice, and ask questions about birth weight, weight
gain and feeding.

A screening test with a specialised light called a transcutaneous bilirubinometer is sometimes used
on your baby’s chest to get an approximate measure of the jaundice.

A blood test to measure the level of bilirubin in your baby’s blood, called serum bilirubin level
(SBR), may be ordered. This is the most accurate way to measure an SBR and involves collecting a
small amount of blood from the arm, hand or heel. Additional blood tests or urine tests may be
ordered if there is evidence your baby’s jaundice is caused by an underlying disorder that will need
treatment.

**Treatment**

Mild jaundice often goes away without treatment, however babies with high levels of bilirubin may
need treatment. Treatment may include phototherapy, exchange transfusion or medication.

## [Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Wearable Digital Phenotyping for Hemodialysis Vascular Access
## Monitoring: From Physical Examination to Home-Based Early Warning][112]

Hemodialysis vascular access is the lifeline of patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis, yet
access dysfunction remains a major cause of inadequate dialysis, repeated intervention, unplanned
catheter use, hospitalization, and eventual access loss. Current vascular access care relies on
physical examination, auscultation, dialysis-machine parameters, access-flow surveillance, duplex
ultrasound, and angiography. Although these approaches remain clinically indispensable, they are
episodic, operator-dependent, and poorly suited for continuous home-based warning. Recent advances
in artificial intelligence, digital auscultation, photoplethysmography, pulse radar sensing, soft
thermal sensors, wireless thrill sensors, ultrasound video analysis, and artificial intelligence of
things systems have created new opportunities to transform vascular access surveillance from
intermittent clinical assessment to continuous digital phenotyping. In this review, we propose a
framework for artificial intelligence–enabled vascular access monitoring organized around four
linked domains: pathophysiological signal generation, sensor-based digital phenotyping, artificial
intelligence–based risk inference, and clinically actionable home-based warning. We summarize recent
evidence from acoustic artificial intelligence, photoplethysmography-based classification, pulse
radar sensing, wearable thermal and vibration sensors, artificial intelligence–assisted ultrasound,
and multimodal clinical risk prediction models across the vascular access life cycle. We further
discuss key barriers to clinical translation, including inconsistent definitions of access
dysfunction, heterogeneous reference standards, small single-center datasets, limited external
validation, device usability, alert fatigue, workflow integration, regulatory requirements, and the

## Get to know Skinsight

 

Skinsight is your gateway to quality skin health information designed to empower everyday people
like you. Presented in an engaging and accessible way, we hope you gain a deeper understanding of
health concerns and find suitable treatment options for your skin-related issues.

Skinsight’s user-friendly interface guides you through the search process, making it easy to
discover relevant information and make well-informed decisions about your skin health. With our
cutting-edge search engine, you can trust the results.

All content on Skinsight is edited and reviewed by physicians and qualified health professionals and
is powered by the team at VisualDx, a trusted software used by clinicians around the world. This
guarantees the credibility and accuracy of the information you access through our platform.

It is important to note that while our content is designed to educate and inform, it should not be
seen as a substitute for professional medical advice. Skinsight is here to complement your health
journey, not replace medical visits. Your well-being is our priority, and we encourage you to
consult with healthcare experts for personalized guidance.

* 100K + Satisfied Customers
* Professional Grade Technology
* 90% Success Rate

## UVB Phototherapy for Chronic Skin Conditions

UV light therapy treats chronic inflammatory and depigmenting skin conditions without any systemic
drug involvement. Narrowband UVB (311–313 nm) targets key pathological processes in the skin.
Psoriatic plaques respond through suppression of hyperproliferative keratinocytes. In atopic
dermatitis, the inflammatory cascade is dampened. Vitiligo lesions show reactivation of melanocyte
function alongside lateral migration into depigmented zones

Sessions take just a few minutes, usually two or three times weekly. The dose moves up as the skin
handles more. Improvement comes in steps, not all at once

Phototherapy’s presence in modern treatment guidelines isn’t the result of a recent trend — the
modality has carried decades of clinical use behind it. The reason is simple: it works across
multiple conditions, and the safety record holds up even over years of use. For patients who need
long-term control of their skin disease but want to avoid systemic drugs or immunosuppression, it’s
often the most reasonable option.

## Types of light

[
01

#### UVA (340–400 nm)

UVA penetrates further into the skin than UVB. That depth makes it useful for deeper-dermis disease
— morphea, scleroderma, T-cell lymphoma, plus eczema cases where UVB failed. Older PUVA protocols
paired UVA with psoralen — a photosensitizing drug — and ran psoriasis treatment for years before
NB-UVB took over.

The modern form is UVA-1 at 340–400 nm. No psoralen, the burning wavelengths are filtered out, and
the dose is kept tight. Mostly used now for connective-tissue and inflammatory disease.

][33]
[
03

#### Excimer Laser (308 nm)

The 308 nm excimer laser is built around a xenon-chloride light source. Output is monochromatic UVB,
applied directly to the lesion via a handpiece. Adjacent healthy skin receives no dose. With energy
concentrated on a small treatment field, per-session fluence can run substantially higher than what
a whole-body NB-UVB cabinet permits — in cabinet-based treatment, healthy tissue caps the maximum
dose.

That usually means a faster response and fewer visits, with less total UV exposure for the patient.
It’s a well-established option in dermatology for localized disease, and FDA-cleared for psoriasis,
vitiligo, and atopic dermatitis.

][34] [
02

#### Narrowband UVB (311–313 nm)

UVB light therapy is the most widely used form of phototherapy in dermatology. Narrowband UVB
(NB-UVB) concentrates light at 311 nm — the specific wavelength shown to clear psoriasis plaques,
repigment vitiligo, and reduce eczema inflammation without the deeper tissue exposure of UVA.

Sessions last seconds to a few minutes. Standard protocols schedule 2–3 sessions weekly across an
8–12 week treatment course. UVB Lamps for Psoriasis and Vitiligo is the clinical standard because it
works across skin types, carries a strong safety profile even with long-term use, and can be
prescribed for treatment at home.

][35]

## Home Phototherapy for Chronic Skin Conditions

Home-based light therapy provides a non-invasive option for managing chronic skin conditions such as
psoriasis, vitiligo, eczema and atopic dermatitis. Treatment is performed under a dermatologist’s
guidance, with protocols adjusted based on skin response and disease type.
* 308 nm Excimer – Targeted UVB treatment delivers high-precision dosing directly to affected areas
  while sparing healthy skin.
* 311 nm Handheld UVB – Uses the same therapeutic wavelength as clinical systems in a compact
  format.

## Home Low-Level Laser Therapy for Hair Growth

LLLT is used to treat androgenetic alopecia in men and women. Red light (≈650 nm) stimulates hair
follicles, supporting the transition to the growth phase and improving hair density over time.

Treatment is delivered through wearable helmet devices designed for consistent at-home use. Sessions

TheraLight is a leader in full-body red light therapy bed innovation, delivering clinically backed
photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT). Each system is designed with advanced LED technology,
customizable pulsing, and multiple therapeutic wavelengths to give your clients results they can
feel.

support, cooling system, and JBL sound, all in one beautifully engineered system.

## Why Choose TheraLight?

### Multi-Wavelength Power

The only full-body red light therapy beds with four independently controlled wavelengths (633, 810,
850, 940 nm)

### Patented LED Tech

Adjustable pulse settings (1–5000 Hz) for customized dosing

### Clinically Proven Benefits

Based on decades of research in red light therapy beds

### Trusted by Providers Nationwide

Over 1,000 systems placed in clinics, spas, and recovery centers

### Lifetime LED Warranty

We stand behind our systems for the long haul

### VIP Installation Service

Further setting us apart from the competition, TheraLight personally delivers and installs each
TheraLight purchase onsite at your location. Our technicians travel around the United States and
World to install each and every light bed. In addition to the installation, our team members train
you and your staff how to properly utilize the device to maximize your patient outcomes. Our
clinical pain management and light therapy experts will guide you through how to deliver the most
successful patient outcomes, as well as financial planning to maximize your ROI.

### On Demand Delivery

We know that time is money and the longer you wait to receive your product, the longer you wait to
receive the benefits; both clinically and financially. So, we ship as soon as you pay! Unlike other
competitors, our products are not built-to-order. Instead, we maintain inventory that is
fully-stocked and ready-to-ship. All TheraLight units can ship within 24 hours of receipt of payment
for a 5–7-day transit time, anywhere in the US. For all international orders, expect an additional
3-5 days of processing.

TheraLight purchase onsite at your location. Our technicians travel around the United States and
World to install each and every light bed. In addition to the installation, our team members train
you and your staff how to properly utilize the device to maximize your patient outcomes. Our
clinical pain management and light therapy experts will guide you through how to deliver the most
successful patient outcomes, as well as financial planning to maximize your ROI.

We know that time is money and the longer you wait to receive your product, the longer you wait to
receive the benefits; both clinically and financially. So, we ship as soon as you pay! Unlike other
competitors, our products are not built-to-order. Instead, we maintain inventory that is
fully-stocked and ready-to-ship. All TheraLight units can ship within 24 hours of receipt of payment
for a 5–7-day transit time, anywhere in the US. For all international orders, expect an additional
3-5 days of processing.

### FAQs

#### [What is light therapy, and how does it help chronic skin conditions at Array Skin?][40]

Light therapy, also known as narrowband UVB phototherapy, uses a precise wavelength of UVB light to
calm inflammation, reduce itching, slow skin cell overgrowth, and stimulate pigment production. It
is a leading treatment for eczema, psoriasis, and vitiligo, offering a safe, drug-free alternative
to topical steroids and systemic medications.

Array Skin began offering narrowband UVB therapy in Orange County and Los Angeles and is expanding
access through franchised clinics in select U.S. markets, bringing this specialized clinical service
to patients who may otherwise face significant barriers to care.

# About Cutaneous Lymphoma

Our Vision
A Life Free From the Burdens of Cutaneous Lymphomas
Welcome to the Cutaneous Lymphoma Foundation where we believe knowledge is power!
WHAT IS CUTANEOUS LYMPHOMA?

Cutaneous lymphomas are cancers of lymphocytes (a type of white blood cells) that primarily involve
the skin. Cutaneous lymphomas are classified based on whether they are cancers of B-lymphocytes
(B-cell) or T-lymphocytes (T-cell).

## CUTANEOUS T-CELL LYMPHOMA (CTCL)

Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) is the most common type of cutaneous lymphoma, and typically
presents with red, scaly patches or plaques on the skin. Itching is common, with more than 80% of
people with CTCL reporting they have itch. CTCL often mimics eczema, psoriasis, or other chronic
dermatitis, and because of this it’s common that the diagnosis of CTCL is delayed, sometimes by
years or decades. Only a minority of people with CTCL develop advanced disease, with tumor
formation, ulceration, involvement of lymph nodes, blood, and internal organs. Most people with CTCL
have indolent (i.e. chronic, slowly growing) lymphomas – treatable, but not curable, and usually not
life-threatening.

## CUTANEOUS B-CELL LYMPHOMAS (CBCL)

Cutaneous B-cell lymphomas (CBCL) make up about 20-25% of all cutaneous lymphomas, and are cancers
that develop from skin-based B-cells.  There are 3 main types of CBCL; primary cutaneous follicle
center (“follicular”) lymphoma, primary cutaneous marginal zone (“MALT”) lymphoma, and primary
cutaneous diffuse large B-cell (DLBCL, “leg type”) lymphoma. Primary cutaneous follicle center and
primary cutaneous marginal zone lymphomas are the most common forms of CBCL, and are slow growing or
indolent types that respond well to mild treatments. Systemic or nodal B-cell lymphomas can
secondarily involve the skin, and when a skin biopsy shows B-cell lymphoma it is very important to
make sure that the lymphoma is truly coming from the skin and not from a systemic lymphoma that has
spread to the skin.  

For a more in depth overview, watch [Cutaneous Lymphoma 101][82].

# Cutaneous T-cell Lymphoma

CTCL stands for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, a rare cancer of T-lymphocytes (a type of white blood
cells) that involves the skin. There are several types of CTCL, but mycosis fungoides and Sézary
syndrome are the most common. We've provided an overview of the disease, treatment and prognosis.

# Mycosis Fungoides

Mycosis fungoides is the most common form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL). Mycosis fungoides”
and “CTCL” are often used interchangeably, which is imprecise, as mycosis fungoides is just one type
of CTCL. Learn more about how it is diagnosed, treated and its prognosis.
* [Read more][84]

# SÉZARY SYNDROME

The two most common types of cutaneous T-cell lymphomas are mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome.
Learn how Sézary syndrome is diagnosed, its treatments and prognosis.
* [Read more][85]

# Primary Cutaneous B-cell Lymphoma

Primary cutaneous B-cell lymphomas (CBCLs) are a cutaneous lymphoma (a cancer of white blood cells)
that affects B-cells in the skin. Learn more about the diagnosis, variants, treatment options and
prognosis of CBCLs.
* [Read more][86]

# Lymphomatoid Papulosis

Lymphomatoid Papulosis (LyP) is a disorder of the immune system that manifests with self-healing
small bumps and spots on the skin that come and go. Learn more about how LyP is diagnosed, treated
and its prognosis.
* [Read more][87]

# PRIMARY CUTANEOUS ANAPLASTIC LARGE CELL LYMPHOMA

Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphomas (CTCL) are part of a group of rare non-Hodgkin lymphomas that
arise from the T-cell type lymphocytes. Learn more about how it is diagnosed, the variants,
treatments and prognosis.
* [Read more][88]

Mycosis fungoides  (MF) is the most common form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Folliculotropic
mycosis fungoides (FMF) is a subtype of MF that involves hair follicles.

# Discover the Power of Light Therapy.

Narrowband ultraviolet B light therapy (NB-UVB) has helped improve the quality of life and outcomes
in patients with chronic skin conditions for decades.  
[Book a 10-Min Discovery Call ][37] [Explore the Science ][38]
discover more [scroll]
[fav]

## 
## Supporting People with Autoimmune Conditions and Skin Disorders Driven by Inflammation

From translational research in acute COVID, MS fatigue, and chronic skin conditions, light therapy
offers a non-drug option your doctor can prescribe to calm your immune system.
* Patients
  If your immune system is in chronic overdrive, light therapy may help.
* Caregivers
  We support your role in guiding care and empowering informed decisions.
* Physicians
  For providers exploring complementary options grounded in research.
[Explore the Science ][39]

## How It Works

Our skin is specifically tuned to absorb NB-UVB light, which starts a natural cascade of actions
that calms the immune system and reduces inflammation for better health. Cytokind partners with you
and your care provider to make this light therapy treatment accessible at home.
* **NB-UVB Safety and Efficacy**
  NB-UVB light therapy has been used safely for decades, with a long track record in dermatology of
  effectively treating many conditions.
* **Prescribed by Your Care Provider**
  The purchase of these lights requires a prescription from your care provider. Cytokind is here to
  help.
[GettyImages-1635844476]
* **What You’ll Experience**
  The therapy starts with very short sessions—usually less than a minute per side each day—and
  gradually increases to about four minutes per side over a month, becoming an easy part of your
  daily routine and ongoing health maintenance.
* Ongoing Support
  From device delivery to daily use, we make sure you’re not on your own.
[Explore the Science ][40]
[GettyImages-1413606459]

* *Provide the power of in-office quality syntonics…in the home.*
* *Our Filters = ****PAQ: ***

* *The instrument contains 8 filter combinations chosen at the touch of the computer tablet. *

  nervous system for added effectiveness. Participants love this! Spitler promoted it!*
* *Pay monthly instead of purchasing. *

  Pi/O, D/O, N. *
* *Designed to attach to any commercially made computer arm.* Choose from a rolling kioske or a
  desktop option.

**Only EyeLux has products being used in university studies.**

The first-ever automatic computerized syntonic instrument. Efficacy and efficiency together.

## אבחון טריקולוגי

השלב הראשון מתחיל באבחון טריקולוגי מקצועי באמצעות מיכשור מתקדם. האבחון אינו פולשני וללא כאבים.
באמצעות בדיקה מיקרוסקופית אנו בודקים את בריאות גוף השיערה, שורש השיערה, בריאות הקרקפת ופרמטרים
נוספים במטרה למפות במדוייק את המצב הקיים ואת הטיפול האפקטיבי הנדרש להשבת בריאות שיערך והכל באופן
מדוייק ומותאם אישית עבורך.

###### Filtration Group

## Discovering new paths to good health

Filtration Group is responsible for breakthrough solutions that advance a healthier society on a
global scale. They purify the air we breathe, filter the water we drink, make our hospitals safer,
reduce carbon emissions and enhance the effectiveness of medical devices. Their solutions protect
our loved ones from harmful elements and give us peace of mind.

###### Task force tips

## Saving Lives and Protecting Property

For as long as there have been fire pumps, firefighters have had difficulty obtaining the correct
pressure from firehoses. Task Force Tips created a nozzle that adapts to varying degrees of pressure
— making it safer and easier for firefighters to do their jobs. It’s a small component that has made
a huge impact and helped countless firefighters save lives.

Wir, die Schulze & Böhm GmbH, sind mit den weltweit führenden medisun UV- und Lichtsystemen seit
über 34 Jahren der Partner für Dermatologen in Praxen und Kliniken. Die umfangreiche Produktpalette
reicht vom kompakten **medisun Psori-Kamm** über verschiedene Teilbestrahlungsgeräte bis zu
anspruchsvollen Ganzkörper-Therapie-Systemen der Extraklasse. Dazu zählen insbesondere die
UV-Kabinen **medisun 2800 Innovation**, die **medisun PDT Systeme** und die **medisun XENIA** UVA-1
Liege mit ihrer innovativen Energiespartechnologie und ihren vielfältigen Funktionen. Nicht nur das
**medisun XENIA UVA-1** System ist weltweit konkurrenzlos, sondern auch viele weitere Innovationen
aus unserem Hause!  Hautkrankheiten, wie Psoriasis, Neurodermitis, Vitiligo, weißer Hautkrebs
(aktinische Keratosen), Sklerodermie und andere Autoimmunerkrankungen, können heute erfolgreich und
optimiert mit medisun-Therapiesystemen behandelt werden. Alle medisun Systeme stammen aus eigener
Entwicklung und werden **„Made in Germany“** in unserem Werk in Brühl produziert. Medisun-Produkte
erfüllen höchste Qualitätsansprüche und sind als Medizinprodukte CE-zertifiziert.

Die Software für die medisun UV- und Lichtsysteme und das netzwerkfähige
Medisoft-Therapiemanagementsystem wird komplett in unserem Haus von erfahrenen Ingenieuren
entwickelt. medisun-Produkte sind weltweit bekannt für hervorragende Behandlungserfolge, einfache
Bedienung und langlebige Qualität.

Kundenservice steht für uns an erster Stelle. Neben unserem werkseigenen Kundendienst stehen Ihnen
auch unsere geschulten Servicepartner in über 34 Ländern zur Verfügung.

Wir sind Ihr kompetenter Ansprechpartner zu allen Themen in der Phototherapie! Für weitere

# Narrowband UVB Phototherapy Treatment: Safe, Effective, & Versatile

Phothera is the leading manufacturer of FDA-cleared home and clinical use narrowband phototherapy
devices for chronic skin conditions. The company was formed through the merger of Daavlin and
National Biological Corporation (NatBio), both unified under [Madison Industries][48] — a global
industrial leader dedicated to building brands that are safer, healthier, and built for long-term
growth. Phothera brings over 80 years of combined phototherapy experience.

## Bring Proven Phototherapy into Modern Dermatology Workflows

Dermatologists have relied on narrowband ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) phototherapy for decades to treat
psoriasis, vitiligo, and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL), where it remains a first-line therapy in
the American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) guidelines. For atopic dermatitis (eczema), phototherapy
is an important option when topical treatments are not enough.

Phothera helps make prescribing and managing phototherapy simple with tools, like convenient EMR
integrations and digital prescription submissions, designed to support you, your practice, and your
patients.

## Why Dermatologists Choose NB-UVB Phototherapy with Phothera

Reduce reliance on systemic medications:

A medication-free treatment option for psoriasis, vitiligo, CTCL, and atopic dermatitis.

Improved adherence with home phototherapy:

Guided Mode devices include protocols with built-in safety guardrails and demonstrated 3x higher
adherence in the 783-patient LITE clinical trial.¹

Simplify prescribing and workflow:

Compatible with Epic and EMA to support prescribing and documentation.

Expanded patient access and coverage:

Broad insurance coverage with $0 cost for eligible patients, helping remove financial barriers to
treatment.

## Phototherapy can be administered in-office or at-home, making it a versatile & widely adaptable
## treatment choice.

* Designed for safe home treatment
* Guided Mode technology with on-device app and** safety protocols built in**
* **3x higher adherence compared with standard home therapy **(LITE Study, n=783)¹
* Broad insurance coverage with **$0 cost for eligible patients***
* **EMR-compatible prescribing with EMA**^{®}**, Epic^{®}, and most other major dermtology EMRs**

*$0 patient cost applies to eligible insured patients. Not all patients will qualify.

* Clinical phototherapy devices designed for dermatology practices
* Also covered by most major insurance providers

The 5-in-1 Benefits of Narrowband Phototherapy

**UNRIVALED SAFETY PROFILE**

Narrowband UVB phototherapy is an ideal first line treatment that is safe for pediatrics², pregnant
women³, geriatics⁴, and immunocompromised patients⁵ and needle-adverse.

Phototherapy’s minimal side effect profile makes it a safer alternative to many systemic
medications.

Research has also shown that Narrowband UVB phototherapy has no significant association with
Malignant Melanoma.

**INDUSTRY LEADING EFFECTIVENESS**

For decades, clinical study data has shown consistently high rates of clearance (95.1% clearance⁵)
for both PUVA and Narrowband UVB phototherapy, with many patients reaching PASI 75 weeks earlier
than the leading biologics.⁵

## About Physiopedia

Physiopedia is the world’s leading online knowledge platform for physiotherapy and rehabilitation
professionals. It brings together evidence-based clinical content, practical resources, and
continuing education to support learning, decision-making, and better patient outcomes. Built and
reviewed by qualified clinicians worldwide, Physiopedia helps students, educators, and practitioners
stay current, confident, and connected in an evolving profession.

## [Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Wearable Digital Phenotyping for Hemodialysis Vascular Access
## Monitoring: From Physical Examination to Home-Based Early Warning][112]

Hemodialysis vascular access is the lifeline of patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis, yet
access dysfunction remains a major cause of inadequate dialysis, repeated intervention, unplanned
catheter use, hospitalization, and eventual access loss. Current vascular access care relies on
physical examination, auscultation, dialysis-machine parameters, access-flow surveillance, duplex
ultrasound, and angiography. Although these approaches remain clinically indispensable, they are
episodic, operator-dependent, and poorly suited for continuous home-based warning. Recent advances
in artificial intelligence, digital auscultation, photoplethysmography, pulse radar sensing, soft
thermal sensors, wireless thrill sensors, ultrasound video analysis, and artificial intelligence of
things systems have created new opportunities to transform vascular access surveillance from
intermittent clinical assessment to continuous digital phenotyping. In this review, we propose a
framework for artificial intelligence–enabled vascular access monitoring organized around four
linked domains: pathophysiological signal generation, sensor-based digital phenotyping, artificial
intelligence–based risk inference, and clinically actionable home-based warning. We summarize recent
evidence from acoustic artificial intelligence, photoplethysmography-based classification, pulse
radar sensing, wearable thermal and vibration sensors, artificial intelligence–assisted ultrasound,
and multimodal clinical risk prediction models across the vascular access life cycle. We further
discuss key barriers to clinical translation, including inconsistent definitions of access
dysfunction, heterogeneous reference standards, small single-center datasets, limited external
validation, device usability, alert fatigue, workflow integration, regulatory requirements, and the
need for prospective outcome-based trials. Future studies should move beyond offline diagnostic
accuracy toward standardized external validation, longitudinal patient-specific baselines,

## Get to know Skinsight

 

Skinsight is your gateway to quality skin health information designed to empower everyday people
like you. Presented in an engaging and accessible way, we hope you gain a deeper understanding of
health concerns and find suitable treatment options for your skin-related issues.

Skinsight’s user-friendly interface guides you through the search process, making it easy to
discover relevant information and make well-informed decisions about your skin health. With our
cutting-edge search engine, you can trust the results.

All content on Skinsight is edited and reviewed by physicians and qualified health professionals and
is powered by the team at VisualDx, a trusted software used by clinicians around the world. This
guarantees the credibility and accuracy of the information you access through our platform.

It is important to note that while our content is designed to educate and inform, it should not be
seen as a substitute for professional medical advice. Skinsight is here to complement your health
journey, not replace medical visits. Your well-being is our priority, and we encourage you to
consult with healthcare experts for personalized guidance.

## UVB Phototherapy for Chronic Skin Conditions

UV light therapy treats chronic inflammatory and depigmenting skin conditions without any systemic
drug involvement. Narrowband UVB (311–313 nm) targets key pathological processes in the skin.
Psoriatic plaques respond through suppression of hyperproliferative keratinocytes. In atopic
dermatitis, the inflammatory cascade is dampened. Vitiligo lesions show reactivation of melanocyte
function alongside lateral migration into depigmented zones

Sessions take just a few minutes, usually two or three times weekly. The dose moves up as the skin
handles more. Improvement comes in steps, not all at once

Phototherapy’s presence in modern treatment guidelines isn’t the result of a recent trend — the
modality has carried decades of clinical use behind it. The reason is simple: it works across
multiple conditions, and the safety record holds up even over years of use. For patients who need
long-term control of their skin disease but want to avoid systemic drugs or immunosuppression, it’s
often the most reasonable option.

## Types of light

[
01

#### UVA (340–400 nm)

UVA penetrates further into the skin than UVB. That depth makes it useful for deeper-dermis disease
— morphea, scleroderma, T-cell lymphoma, plus eczema cases where UVB failed. Older PUVA protocols
paired UVA with psoralen — a photosensitizing drug — and ran psoriasis treatment for years before
NB-UVB took over.

The modern form is UVA-1 at 340–400 nm. No psoralen, the burning wavelengths are filtered out, and
the dose is kept tight. Mostly used now for connective-tissue and inflammatory disease.

][33]
[
03

#### Excimer Laser (308 nm)

The 308 nm excimer laser is built around a xenon-chloride light source. Output is monochromatic UVB,
applied directly to the lesion via a handpiece. Adjacent healthy skin receives no dose. With energy
concentrated on a small treatment field, per-session fluence can run substantially higher than what
a whole-body NB-UVB cabinet permits — in cabinet-based treatment, healthy tissue caps the maximum
dose.

That usually means a faster response and fewer visits, with less total UV exposure for the patient.
It’s a well-established option in dermatology for localized disease, and FDA-cleared for psoriasis,
vitiligo, and atopic dermatitis.

][34] [
02

#### Narrowband UVB (311–313 nm)

UVB light therapy is the most widely used form of phototherapy in dermatology. Narrowband UVB
(NB-UVB) concentrates light at 311 nm — the specific wavelength shown to clear psoriasis plaques,
repigment vitiligo, and reduce eczema inflammation without the deeper tissue exposure of UVA.

Sessions last seconds to a few minutes. Standard protocols schedule 2–3 sessions weekly across an
8–12 week treatment course. UVB Lamps for Psoriasis and Vitiligo is the clinical standard because it
works across skin types, carries a strong safety profile even with long-term use, and can be
prescribed for treatment at home.

][35]

## Home Phototherapy for Chronic Skin Conditions

Home-based light therapy provides a non-invasive option for managing chronic skin conditions such as
psoriasis, vitiligo, eczema and atopic dermatitis. Treatment is performed under a dermatologist’s
guidance, with protocols adjusted based on skin response and disease type.
* 308 nm Excimer – Targeted UVB treatment delivers high-precision dosing directly to affected areas
  while sparing healthy skin.
* 311 nm Handheld UVB – Uses the same therapeutic wavelength as clinical systems in a compact
  format.

## UVB Phototherapy for Chronic Skin Conditions

UV light therapy treats chronic inflammatory and depigmenting skin conditions without any systemic
drug involvement. Narrowband UVB (311–313 nm) targets key pathological processes in the skin.
Psoriatic plaques respond through suppression of hyperproliferative keratinocytes. In atopic
dermatitis, the inflammatory cascade is dampened. Vitiligo lesions show reactivation of melanocyte
function alongside lateral migration into depigmented zones

Sessions take just a few minutes, usually two or three times weekly. The dose moves up as the skin
handles more. Improvement comes in steps, not all at once

Phototherapy’s presence in modern treatment guidelines isn’t the result of a recent trend — the
modality has carried decades of clinical use behind it. The reason is simple: it works across
multiple conditions, and the safety record holds up even over years of use. For patients who need
long-term control of their skin disease but want to avoid systemic drugs or immunosuppression, it’s
often the most reasonable option.

## Types of light

[
01

#### UVA (340–400 nm)

UVA penetrates further into the skin than UVB. That depth makes it useful for deeper-dermis disease
— morphea, scleroderma, T-cell lymphoma, plus eczema cases where UVB failed. Older PUVA protocols
paired UVA with psoralen — a photosensitizing drug — and ran psoriasis treatment for years before
NB-UVB took over.

The modern form is UVA-1 at 340–400 nm. No psoralen, the burning wavelengths are filtered out, and
the dose is kept tight. Mostly used now for connective-tissue and inflammatory disease.

][33]
[
03

#### Excimer Laser (308 nm)

The 308 nm excimer laser is built around a xenon-chloride light source. Output is monochromatic UVB,
applied directly to the lesion via a handpiece. Adjacent healthy skin receives no dose. With energy
concentrated on a small treatment field, per-session fluence can run substantially higher than what
a whole-body NB-UVB cabinet permits — in cabinet-based treatment, healthy tissue caps the maximum
dose.

That usually means a faster response and fewer visits, with less total UV exposure for the patient.
It’s a well-established option in dermatology for localized disease, and FDA-cleared for psoriasis,
vitiligo, and atopic dermatitis.

][34] [
02

#### Narrowband UVB (311–313 nm)

UVB light therapy is the most widely used form of phototherapy in dermatology. Narrowband UVB
(NB-UVB) concentrates light at 311 nm — the specific wavelength shown to clear psoriasis plaques,
repigment vitiligo, and reduce eczema inflammation without the deeper tissue exposure of UVA.

Sessions last seconds to a few minutes. Standard protocols schedule 2–3 sessions weekly across an
8–12 week treatment course. UVB Lamps for Psoriasis and Vitiligo is the clinical standard because it
works across skin types, carries a strong safety profile even with long-term use, and can be
prescribed for treatment at home.

][35]

## Home Phototherapy for Chronic Skin Conditions

Home-based light therapy provides a non-invasive option for managing chronic skin conditions such as
psoriasis, vitiligo, eczema and atopic dermatitis. Treatment is performed under a dermatologist’s
guidance, with protocols adjusted based on skin response and disease type.
* 308 nm Excimer – Targeted UVB treatment delivers high-precision dosing directly to affected areas
  while sparing healthy skin.
* 311 nm Handheld UVB – Uses the same therapeutic wavelength as clinical systems in a compact
  format.

## Home Low-Level Laser Therapy for Hair Growth

LLLT is used to treat androgenetic alopecia in men and women. Red light (≈650 nm) stimulates hair
follicles, supporting the transition to the growth phase and improving hair density over time.

Treatment is delivered through wearable helmet devices designed for consistent at-home use. Sessions
are typically performed several times per week, with results developing gradually over 3–6 months.

#### Reflectance Confocal Microscopy (RCM)

Reflectance confocal microscopy enables non-invasive imaging of skin at near-cellular resolution in
real time. Used to evaluate pigmented lesions, support melanoma detection, and guide treatment
planning — and it reduces unnecessary biopsies.

LED light works in the visible and near-infrared range, with no UV component. Applied for acne
management, skin rejuvenation, wound healing, and post-procedure recovery. Multi-wavelength systems
